description: We are a team of passionate developers who love to build things that actually work. We are strong in AI, full stack, backend systems and creative problem solving. We are doing NASA Space Apps to challenge ourselves, use real NASA data and build something meaningful. We are looking for curious, committed people who are ready to bring fresh ideas to the table. You don’t have to know everything, just be willing to learn, build and contribute.
summary:
Parallax asks a simple question: what if a flood map does not show the whole flood? We developed a web application that uses NISAR L-band radar to investigate possible flood inundation beneath vegetation, where optical imagery and some other sensors can struggle, and compares the result with NASA OPERA DSWx surface-water maps.

NISAR GCOV data is converted to georeferenced rasters, aligned on a common grid and compared with a pre-event baseline to find two signatures: darkening consistent with open water, and brightening in vegetation that may indicate flooded vegetation. Areas our radar flags as water-like but OPERA does not map as water are shown as "gaps": a disagreement in mapped evidence, not confirmed floodwater. OPERA is used as a reference, not ground truth.

Every candidate links to a "how we know" evidence panel with scene IDs, dates, measurements and cautions. Users can explore, compare before and after, inspect evidence and export results.

Parallax makes radar flood evidence understandable for analysts, planners and students, and turns sensor disagreement into a clear, auditable starting point for investigation.
details:
Parallax: "See beyond the visible."

WHAT IT DOES

What if a flood map does not show the whole flood? Parallax is a web application that investigates possible flood inundation beneath vegetation using NISAR L-band radar, then compares its findings with NASA OPERA DSWx surface-water maps. Where our radar-derived candidate water is not mapped as water by OPERA, we call it a "gap": a disagreement in mapped evidence, not confirmed extra floodwater. OPERA is treated as a reference, not ground truth.

HOW IT WORKS

We convert NISAR L2 GCOV data (via ASF) from HDF5 to georeferenced GeoTIFF, align scenes on a common grid with quality masks, build a pre-event baseline and compute signed backscatter change in dB. We look for a dual signature: darkening consistent with open water, and brightening in vegetated areas that may indicate flooded vegetation (double-bounce scattering). Land cover helps separate plausible candidates from urban and agricultural confounders. Candidate areas are then compared with OPERA and classed as Agreement, Additional candidate, Reference-only water or Unknown, and we report gap area (km²) and gap fraction.

THE APP

Four views: Explore (study area and sources), Compare (before/after radar swipe with OPERA and gap overlays), Inspect (a "how we know" evidence panel for every polygon: scene IDs, dates, dB change, vegetation class, quality flags and cautions) and Export (GeoJSON, CSV statistics and a short report).

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Parallax helps GIS and disaster analysts find places that deserve a closer look, helps planning and resilience teams prioritize areas for investigation (not evacuation guidance), and helps students and researchers learn radar interpretation and reproduce the analysis.

TOOLS

Data: NISAR GCOV, NASA OPERA DSWx, land cover. Processing: Python, h5py, Rasterio, GDAL, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-image, asf_search/earthaccess. App: FastAPI, React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL JS, GeoJSON and XYZ map tiles.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Parallax treats sensor disagreement as a question to investigate, not a claim. It is evidence-first: every polygon links back to its source scenes, statistics and quality flags, and each result is labelled Observed, Derived, Inferred or Demonstration. A sensitivity analysis shows which findings are stable and which depend on threshold choices. We use transparent, rule-based methods rather than black-box models, so every step can be audited and reproduced.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Honesty about uncertainty: we make no accuracy claims without independent labels, never count missing OPERA pixels as non-water, flag confounders (urban double bounce, crop cycles, soil moisture, terrain), use one consistent colour stretch for before/after imagery, and check scene compatibility before analysis. The case is cached so the demo works offline.

Data credits: NASA, ISRO (NISAR mission), Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF), NASA OPERA.
